title: Orchestrated VPC topology module: subnet roles, NAT/IGW selection, endpoints & routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Scope: build a composable Terraform module to provision opinionated VPC topology for Private deployments: segregated subnets by role (public/bastion, app/private, infra/egress), per-AZ NAT gateway or shared egress pattern based on cost profile, Internet Gateway for public subnets, route tables with explicit associations, interface and gateway endpoints (S3, ECR, STS, CloudWatch Logs), VPC Endpoint policies, and automated health checks and remediation hooks for NAT/IGW availability. Goals: 1) Provide a single, well-documented module that can be included by Private deployment stacks; 2) Offer safe defaults for production (multi-AZ, explicit route table naming, Terraform state migration helpers); 3) Support an upgrade path between major module versions without downtime (canary apply guidance + state migration); 4) Emit metrics and status outputs used by console/observability.
design_notes: Module API will favor declarative role-based 'subnet_roles' map instead of fixed subnet count. Example var: subnet_roles = { control = {cidr_mask=24, share_across_az=false}, app = {cidr_mask=22, share_across_az=true} }. NAT strategy: an enum var nat_mode = [per_az | centralized | none] with explicit cost/latency trade-offs in docs. Endpoint pattern: create gateway endpoints for S3/DynamoDB when request_managed_endpoints = true to avoid cross-AZ data transfer. For interface endpoints, generate security group and allow only designated ENIs. Route tables per role with tags for tracing. Health checks: use Lambda + EventBridge to periodically verify NAT gateway state, route table propagation, and endpoint DNS resolution; expose boolean outputs nat_egress_ok / endpoints_ok and a tf output 'health_checks_arn' for downstream automation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Module can create VPC with role-based subnets across 3 AZs by default. 2) nat_mode=per_az creates NAT gateways in each AZ and associated route tables. 3) nat_mode=centralized creates one egress TGW-style pattern with corresponding routes and alerts if AZ isolation needed. 4) Module outputs route table IDs, endpoint IDs, and a simple JSON status string. 5) Terraform plan shows no destructive default changes when toggling optional features. 6) Example stacks in /examples pass automated terratest suite in CI.
upgrade_and_migration_plan: Major-version bump required for API changes (eg. renaming 'public_subnets' -> 'subnet_roles'). Provide a migration script in examples/migrations/migrate_v1_to_v2.sh that: 1) pins old module, runs terraform state mv commands to rename resources, 2) applies the new module in a canary stack (single AZ), 3) runs health checks and smoke tests, 4) progressively applies to remaining AZs. Release README will have explicit steps and a checklist for safety (snapshot state, backup remote state, disable autoscaling during network changes). CI will run a drift-detection job post-upgrade.
implementation_plan: 1) Terraform 1.4+ with AWS provider >= 5.0 constraint; lock provider versions. 2) Start with core resources: vpc, subnets, route tables, igw, nat gateways. 3) Implement endpoints (gateway + interface) with optional creation by role. 4) Add health check Lambda and IAM role; deploy as optional resource behind 'health_checks_enabled' flag. 5) Write terratest suite covering creation, update (nat_mode switch), and deletion. 6) Add example stacks: a) default multi-AZ, b) cost-optimized centralized NAT, c) air-gapped variant (no internet gateway or interface endpoints). 7) Add docs for upgrade and state migration. 8) Add module to terraform registry and bootstrap automated compatibility tests in GitHub Actions.
security_considerations: - Endpoint policies must follow least privilege: allow only service actions necessary for Private control plane. - Interface endpoints will use dedicated security groups with ingress locked to allowed VPC CIDRs and service IPs. - The health-check Lambda will run with narrow IAM permissions and write only to a dedicated CloudWatch log group. - Sensitive outputs (if any) must be suppressed and instead surfaced via Console signals. - Require security review prior to release; flag set to true.
ci_and_testing: - GitHub Actions workflow 'module-test' will run terraform fmt/tflint, unit plan checks (using checkov), and terratest in ephemeral AWS accounts. - Add a nightly integration job that runs the canary upgrade path and validates health outputs. - Add a policy-as-code scan for endpoint policies and SGs.
